lesson.title: 1. A film everyone talks about
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Jake and Emily are colleagues. On Monday morning, Emily asks Jake about his weekend.*
lines: How was your weekend? Did you do anything fun?
Not really. I **stayed in** and finally watched *Train to Busan*. Everyone’s been telling me to watch it.
Oh, I love that film. Was it **as good as people said?**

Definitely. I’m not really **into** zombie films, but this one has a really good **plot**. **The main character** is a dad who’s always **busy with work**. On his daughter’s birthday, he takes her on a train to Busan to see her mum.
And then the zombies get on the train.
Yeah, and **from then on**, it’s really **fast-paced**. But what I liked most is how the dad slowly **changes from** a **selfish** man **into** a really **caring** father.
Gong Yoo **gives a great performance** in that role.
**The whole cast** is great, actually. The guy who **plays** the strong husband is so **tough** in the **action scenes**, but he also has some of **the funniest lines**.
He’s my **favourite character**. Did you find it scary?
Very. The zombies **look so real**. I **jumped out of my seat** a few times, and in **the scene where** they walk through a train full of zombies, I was **holding my breath** the whole time.
But the ending was so sad.
**Don’t remind me.** When the dad says goodbye to his daughter, I **couldn’t stop crying**. I had to **pause** it for a minute.
**Same here.** I watched it at the cinema, and everyone around me was **in tears**.
The only thing I didn’t like was **the villain**, that selfish businessman. He was so **annoying** that I wanted to throw something at the TV.
Haha, that means the actor **did a good job**. There’s **a sequel** too, but honestly, it’s **not as good as the original**.

lesson.title: 2. A book that stays with you
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Hà’s English colleague, Tom, sees an old Vietnamese novel on her desk at lunchtime.*
lines: It’s *Tắt đèn*, by Ngô Tất Tố. It’s **a Vietnamese classic**. We had to read it at school, and I wanted to read it again **now that I’m older**.
What’s it about? **The cover** looks a bit gloomy.
It’s quite a sad story. It’s **set in** a poor village in northern Vietnam in the 1930s, when Vietnam was **a French colony**.
I don’t know much about **that period**. Was life hard back then?
Very hard, especially for farmers. They had to pay a lot of **tax** every year, **even when** they had nothing to eat.
So is **the main character** a farmer?
Yes, a farmer’s wife called Chị Dậu. Her husband is very ill, and they **don’t have enough money to** pay the tax, so the village officials **take him away** and beat him.
That’s terrible. What does she do?
She **tries everything** to find the money. **In the end**, she **has to** sell her seven-year-old daughter to a rich family.

I know. But my **favourite chapter** is when the officials come back for her husband. At first, she asks them **politely** to **leave him alone**, but they don’t listen, so she gets angry and **fights back**.
Good for her. She sounds really **brave**.
She is. We even have a saying for it: *tức nước vỡ bờ*. It means that if you push people too far, they’ll fight back.
**It sounds like** the book really **shows how hard life was** for ordinary people **under French rule**. Is there an English translation? I’d like to read it.
I think so. I’ll **look it up** for you.

homework.title: Part 2: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to a short film review, then do Parts A and B.

script.text: Hi, and welcome to Film Friday. Today I want to talk about an old favourite: Home Alone. It came out in ==1990==, but ==my family still watches it together every Christmas==.

The main character is Kevin, an ==eight==-year-old boy from a big family. The night before a family trip to Paris, Kevin gets into trouble and has to sleep alone in the attic. ==The next morning, everyone wakes up late and rushes to the airport. In the end, they fly to France without him.==

==At first, Kevin is really happy.== He eats junk food, watches films and jumps on his parents' bed. But then two ==burglars== try to break into the house, and Kevin decides to protect it on his own. He sets up lots of funny ==traps==, and the second half of the film is really fast-paced.

When I was a kid, the traps were my favourite part. ==Now that I'm older, I like a different part: Kevin's mum. She tries everything to get home to her son==, and she even travels across the country in a ==van== with a band. That part always makes me a bit emotional.
There's also an old neighbour who all the kids are scared of. I won't give it away, but ==he's not the person Kevin thinks he is==.
My only problem is the burglars. ==They get hurt so many times that it becomes a bit silly.== Still, it's the perfect Christmas film. ==Nine== out of ten from me.

questions.q: Why does the speaker watch Home Alone every year?
options: It’s something her family does together at Christmas.
It’s always on TV in December.
questions.why: “My family still watches it together every Christmas.”

questions.q: Why is Kevin left at home?
options: His parents think he is too young to travel.
He hides in the attic because he doesn’t want to go.
His family is in a hurry and forgets about him.
questions.why: “Everyone wakes up late and rushes to the airport. In the end, they fly to France without him.”

questions.q: How does Kevin feel when he first finds out he is alone?
Which part of the film does the speaker like most now?
options: The traps Kevin sets for the burglars
The way Kevin’s mum tries to get back to him
The scenes of the family in Paris
questions.why: “Now that I’m older, I like a different part: Kevin’s mum. She tries everything to get home to her son.”

questions.q: What do we learn about the old neighbour?
options: He is one of the burglars.
Kevin has the wrong idea about him.
He travels home with Kevin’s mum.
questions.why: “He’s not the person Kevin thinks he is.”

questions.q: What doesn’t the speaker like about the film?
questions.why: “They get hurt so many times that it becomes a bit silly.”
